taxes.base: Wages, salaries, business and professional income, rents and other income of individuals; employers and payers withhold most of it.
taxes.payer: Individuals; employers withhold it from pay.

rate.headline: 15% to 40% (scale for 2026)
details: Scale for non-employment income in 2026: 15% up to TRY 190,000; 20% to 400,000; 27% to 1,500,000; 35% to 5,300,000; 40% above. There are no local taxes on personal income in Türkiye (PwC).
The scale for 2025, the year of the revenue, was different.
As summarised by PwC (review of 9 September 2026), not checked against the Revenue Administration.

instruments.explanation: The largest tax in the central budget: 25% of its tax revenue in 2025, and up 84% on 2024 in the report.

rate.headline: 25% (30% in the financial sector)
details: Article 32 of the Corporate Tax Law sets 25% for corporations other than those in the financial sector, and 30% for financial sector companies; a domestic minimum tax of 10% applies from 1 January 2025 (PwC).
As summarised by PwC (review of 9 September 2026), not checked against the Revenue Administration.

names.official: Value added tax on domestic transactions

taxes.base: Deliveries of goods and services in Türkiye.
taxes.payer: Consumers; businesses charge it and offset input VAT.

rate.headline: 20% general; reduced rates from 1% to 10%
details: VAT rates vary from 1% to 20% and the general rate is 20% (PwC).
As summarised by PwC (review of 9 September 2026), not checked against the Revenue Administration.

instruments.explanation: The report separates VAT on domestic transactions from VAT on imports.

taxes.base: The customs value of imports plus duties and taxes.

rate.headline: The same rates as the domestic VAT
details: Collected at the border; offset as input VAT by registered importers (PwC).
As summarised by PwC (review of 9 September 2026), not checked against the Revenue Administration.

instruments.explanation: TRY 1.7 trillion in 2025: larger than the VAT on domestic transactions (TRY 1.6 trillion).

taxes.base: Four product groups: petroleum products, natural gas and lubricants; automobiles and other vehicles; tobacco and alcoholic beverages; luxury products.
taxes.payer: Producers and importers; charged once, passed on in the price.

rate.headline: By product group
details: There are four main product groups subject to the special consumption tax at different rates, depending on the tariff number; unlike VAT it is charged only once (PwC).
As summarised by PwC (review of 9 September 2026), not checked against the Revenue Administration.

instruments.explanation: TRY 2.0 trillion: the second-largest line. It covers fuels, vehicles, tobacco, alcohol and luxury goods.

taxes.base: The receipts of banks, insurers and similar institutions from their transactions, as the name of the tax says.

rate.headline: Set by the Banking and Insurance Transactions Tax Law
details: The rate is not extracted here.

taxes.base: Documents such as contracts, wage payrolls and financial papers, as listed in the Stamp Tax Law.

rate.headline: A percentage of the amount stated in the document
details: The rate is not extracted here.

taxes.base: Fees for official services, as the budget classifies them among tax revenues.

rate.headline: Set by the Fees Law
details: The report does not itemise them.

instruments.explanation: TRY 337 billion in 2025, up 62% in the report.

taxes.base: The remaining tax revenues of the central budget; the monthly report gives them as one line and does not itemise them.

rate.headline: Various
details: The detailed budget statistics of the Accounting Directorate name the individual taxes; they were not retrieved for this folio.

instruments.explanation: TRY 593 billion: 5% of the tax revenue.
